01 · About me

Experimental biology with a translational focus.

I am a Molecular Biotechnology graduate with an MSc with Distinction and research experience spanning nanoparticle-based cancer drug delivery, human iPSC-derived cardiomyocyte disease modelling, recombinant protein expression and molecular biology. Alongside laboratory research, I am developing computational biology skills through independent analysis of public datasets using R. I also enjoy science communication and making complex biotechnology more accessible through educational content.

PROJECT 01 · CURRENT RESEARCH

Nanoparticle Drug Delivery in Breast and Lung Cancer

Canterbury Christ Church University · Discovery Park

Research into nanoparticle-based delivery of anticancer compounds in breast and lung cancer models, combining cell-based experiments with the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model and molecular analysis.

  • Mammalian cancer cell culture under CL2 conditions.
  • Sample handling and comparisons across treatment groups.
  • RNA extraction, RT-qPCR and gene-expression analysis.
  • CAM model-related work and tumour/tissue analysis.
Cancer BiologyNanoparticlesCAM ModelRT-qPCR
PROJECT 02 · MSc DISSERTATION

Voltage–Calcium Uncoupling in ACTN2 M228T Cardiomyocytes

University of Birmingham · Dissertation mark: 79/100

My MSc dissertation examined how the ACTN2 p.Met228Thr (M228T) variant affects electrical activity and calcium handling in human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes, using optical mapping and RT-qPCR to investigate mechanisms relevant to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

  • hiPSC culture and cardiomyocyte differentiation using established protocols.
  • Fluorescence-based optical mapping of action potentials and calcium transients.
  • RT-qPCR and interpretation of electrophysiological measures.
hiPSC-CMsOptical MappingRT-qPCRCardiac Disease

PROJECT 04 · INDEPENDENT BIOINFORMATICS

VEGFA, PCNA and Doxorubicin Response

DepMap Public 25Q2 + PRISM Repurposing Secondary Screen 20Q2 · R

Explored whether baseline VEGFA and PCNA expression are associated with sensitivity to free doxorubicin across public cancer cell-line datasets. Expression and drug-response records were matched by DepMap cell-line ID.

  • Joined gene-expression and drug-response data for 461 cell lines.
  • Calculated Spearman correlations overall and in breast and lung subsets.
  • Adjusted p-values using the Benjamini–Hochberg method.
RDepMapPRISMSpearman Correlation

View code, methods and figures on GitHub ↗

Exploratory results relate to free doxorubicin and do not establish how nanoparticle formulations behave.

PROJECT 05 · UNDERGRADUATE DISSERTATION

Total Cyanogens in Cassava Tubers, Leaves and Rind

BSc Biochemistry · University of Calicut · Best Project Award

Collaborative undergraduate research comparing cyanogen content in cassava plant parts collected from local farmers in Pulpally, Wayanad, with a food-safety focus.

  • Comparison of cassava tubers, leaves and rind.
  • Linamarase preparation and spectrophotometric cyanide analysis.
  • Consideration of food safety and community relevance.

PROJECT 06 · PROTEIN BIOTECHNOLOGY

Optimising Soluble GFP Expression in E. coli

Recombinant protein expression and optimisation

A model-protein project exploring expression conditions in E. coli, using fluorescence, protein quantification and gel-based analysis to assess outcomes.

  • Considered IPTG, induction density and temperature.
  • Used Bradford assay, SDS-PAGE and fluorescence measurements.
  • Applied R-based response surface methodology to explore parameter interactions.
Protein ExpressionSDS-PAGER
Research spotlight · Public-data analysis

What did the doxorubicin analysis show?

The analysis did not find statistically significant evidence that baseline VEGFA or PCNA expression predicts free-doxorubicin sensitivity in the overall dataset or in the breast and lung subsets. The plots below are generated from the project's public-data analysis.

461 cell linesMatched expression and drug-response records
Not significantVEGFA and PCNA associations with IC50 after testing
ExploratoryDoes not test nanoparticle-delivered doxorubicin

Key interpretation

Across all cell lines, VEGFA had a Spearman correlation of ρ = 0.054 (adjusted p = 0.249), while PCNA had ρ = −0.082 (adjusted p = 0.157). Within breast and lung subsets, neither gene showed a statistically significant association after adjustment. A negative PCNA trend in the breast subset (ρ = −0.414; adjusted p = 0.248; n = 21) was not statistically significant and should be interpreted cautiously.

Among the three cell lines of particular interest, MDA-MB-231 had the lowest IC50 (0.148 µM), followed by MCF-7 (0.191 µM), while NCI-H358 had the highest (0.494 µM). With only three selected lines, this is descriptive rather than conclusive.

05 · Research outputs

Presentations, writing and conferences

FEATURED PRESENTATION

ELRIG Drug Discovery 2026

Presented research evaluating mesoporous silica nanoparticles loaded with doxorubicin and withaferin A in breast and lung cancer models. The work examined cell viability, CAM tumour growth, angiogenesis and the expression of VEGFA and PCNA. The poster reports reduced tumour growth and angiogenesis/proliferation with nanoparticle-based treatments, with particularly encouraging effects in the lung cancer model.

13–15 October 2026 · ExCeL London
